item.title: Travis Hunter got a lot more work on the defensive side of the ball in Week 3
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In Week 2, Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter had only 31 defensive snaps.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 2, Jaguars cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter had only 31 defensive snaps. As expected, he got a lot more in Week 3.

Hunter was on the field for 45 defensive plays, in a game that featured his first career interception.

On offense, he continues to not do much. After getting six snaps in Week 2, he got only five in Week 3. He was targeted in neither game.

And so it seems as if the Jaguars are moving him toward being a full-time cornerback, and a very part-time receiver.

Whether that means he has accepted his apparent fate remains to be seen. He wants to play both sides of the ball. He wants to have the ball in his hands. And he seems to be concerned that, if he plays only defense and successfully locks down half of the field, he'll rarely touch the ball.

Regardless, his long-term best interests could be best served by playing only defense. Especially since the Jaguars have a great collection of receivers.

item.title: Chop Robinson: Not sure why I got called for roughing Patrick Mahomes, but I had to play on
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson is not complaining about the controversial penalty he got for roughing Patrick Mahomes on Sunday, but he is wondering what he could have done differently.
item.content:encoded:
Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson is not complaining about the controversial penalty he got for roughing Patrick Mahomes on Sunday, but he is wondering what he could have done differently.

Asked what he could have done to avoid the roughing penalty, which the officials said was for landing on Mahomes with his body weight, Robinson said he doesn't know.

"I'm honestly not too sure, but either way, that's what they called, so that's what we got to play on. Next play," Robinson said.

Robinson put his hands down to break his own fall on top of Mahomes, but he said he'll try to do that earlier in the process of falling to the ground next time.

"Just put my hands out earlier, but it's a football play. That's what the refs called, so I had to move on from it," Robinson said. "That's what I could do better on that play, but that's what they called, and that's what it is."

Asked about practicing hitting quarterbacks without landing on them, Robinson said that's a hard thing to do because defensive players don't hit quarterbacks in practice.

"I don't know, that's a hard question. When you can't really work it, you can't hit a quarterback in practice. But I did what I was taught and told to do, and that's what they called, so that's what it is," Robinson said.

The penalty was very costly for the Dolphins, as it came after Mahomes had thrown an incompletion in his own end zone on third down. If not for the penalty, the Chiefs would have punted from deep in their own territory, and the Dolphins would have taken over in good field position while trailing 14-10 in the third quarter. Instead, the 15-yard penalty and automatic first down kept alive a Chiefs drive that ended up lasting 13 plays, covering 80 yards, and ending with a field goal that gave the Chiefs a 17-10 lead in the fourth quarter.

"Of course we wanted to keep them in the end zone, but again, that's what they called. There's nothing I could do about it, just play the next play, and just try to stop them, get the ball back to the offense," Robinson said.

The penalty was one of the biggest plays of the game, and one that Robinson isn't sure how he could have avoided.

item.title: Ben Johnson: Case Keenum's touchdown run was a "Mike Martz special" play call
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears head coach Ben Johnson has earned a reputation as an offensive innovator, but he didn't come up with the idea that led to one of his team's touchdowns in Monday's 27-7 win over the Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
Bears head coach Ben Johnson has earned a reputation as an offensive innovator, but he didn't come up with the idea that led to one of his team's touchdowns in Monday's 27-7 win over the Eagles.

Quarterback Case Keenum ran for a one-yard score in the fourth quarter on a play that saw the two Chicago guards pull in opposite directions while Keenum followed center Garrett Bradbury up the middle for the score. After the game, Johnson credited former Rams head coach Mike Martz with coming up with the play design.

“That’s a Mike Martz special right there, that's the old sucker sneak," Johnson said. "I think they were a little bit tight initially and then they stemmed out at the last second, which gave us the green light to get to that play. It’s an old play, an old but a good play right there.”

Martz memorably called the play during Super Bowl XXXVI and it resulted in a Kurt Warner touchdown run. Johnson was a teenager when that game was played, but Martz's ingenuity stuck with him.

item.title: T.J. Edwards got nothing from eavesdropping on Eagles' huddle
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Monday night's game between the Eagles and Bears featured a moment in which former Eagles (now Bears) linebacker T.J.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game between the Eagles and Bears featured a moment in which former Eagles (now Bears) linebacker T.J. Edwards tiptoed toward the huddle to try to hear what Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was saying.

Then the play started, and Edwards intercepted a pass from Hurts.

After the game, Edwards was asked whether he picked anything up from his eavesdropping attempt.

"No," Edwards said, via Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic. "I was like, 'Maybe I'll hear some familiar stuff,' and like they must have changed language up because I had no idea what they were talking about."

That's no surprise. Edwards last played for the Eagles in 2022. They've had four offensive coordinators since Edwards left.

Regardless, Edwards brings to the Bears a knowledge of Hurts and other players with whom he played. It's one of the basic realities of today's high-mobility NFL. Little things can be picked up and possibly used later. Tendencies, tells, habits, etc.

Every quarterback needs to be keeping notes on all defenders he faces in practice, and every defender needs to be keeping notes on all quarterbacks they face in practice. Today's coworker can be tomorrow's enemy, and an edge can come from anywhere.

item.title: Ben Johnson takes another dig at Jared Goff's mobility
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When Bears coach Ben Johnson compared the mobility of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lack of mobility of Jared Goff in 2025, Johnson promptly explained he wasn't taking a shot at Goff.
item.content:encoded:
When Bears coach Ben Johnson compared the mobility of quarterback Caleb Williams to the lack of mobility of Jared Goff in 2025, Johnson promptly explained he wasn't taking a shot at Goff.

"It was not a shot at Jared," Johnson said in early 2025. "I’ve talked to Jared about it. Sometimes your comments get skewed a little bit. That was not my intent. He certainly understands that. It was more directed towards Caleb and what he brings to the table."

Fast forward to last night, and Johnson took another apparent shot at Goff.

"Well, I've got a little history with that, of calling plays for someone not so mobile," Johnson said regarding the different playing styles of Williams and Case Keenum.

Johnson likely will say again that it wasn't a shot at Goff. And it really isn't. Everyone knows Jared Goff isn't Usain Bolt.

Still, watch the video. Johnson knew what was coming. And he smirked a couple of times while the question was being asked. He knew exactly what he was going to say. And he seemed to enjoy it.

There's a refreshing cheekiness to Johnson that often shines through. Indeed, Johnson added another remark about the fact that, for the first time in his career as a play-caller, he was working with someone who wasn't the first overall pick in the draft.

"Now, I don't have a history with someone that's not a number one pick though," Johnson said after his latest non-shot shot at Goff. "So that was apparently a big deal."

It wasn't necessarily a "big deal." But it was, you know, a fact. The latest fact is that it doesn't matter, and that Johnson was able to take a guy who hadn't played in a regular-season game in 1,009 days and make him look like a Pro Bowler.

It's no surprise, given that Johnson took a guy the Rams couldn't wait to get rid of and turned him into a high-end starter.

item.title: Jerry Jones: No explanation for end of Ravens loss that you're satisfied with
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' chances of winning Sunday's game against the Ravens in Brazil unraveled in the final seconds of the fourth quarter.

After the team used its final timeout after a short run by quarterback Dak Prescott on second down from the 5-yard-line, they dialed up a pass play that appeared to get wide receiver George Pickens open in the end zone. Prescott threw the ball away as Pickens got free, which both he and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said was by design after the game.

During a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked about the sequence from the timing of the timeout through Prescott's throw.

“There’s no explanation that you’re satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let’s be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they’re satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time, there’s no question about it. There’s no explanation. There’s an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. We can’t get that back. No way to get it back. What you can do is use it — if there’s any aspect of it that you want to just not even think happened. Any aspect of it, use it to get better.”

The Cowboys settled for a field goal with seven seconds left, which turned out to be just enough time for the Ravens to set up a 56-yard game-winning field goal of their own. The handling of the kickoff, which went for a touchback that took no time off the clock, was another matter lacking a satisfying rationale that might make the loss sit better with anyone.

item.title: Andy Reid: I'll let you know when Josh Simmons is coming back
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have started the season 3-0 despite not having their starting left tackle available.

Josh Simmons has been sidelined by a back injury that’s been considered week-to-week. But it’s currently unclear if Simmons will return to practice in advance of Sunday’s matchup with the 3-0 Raiders.

“I'll tell you what, I will let you guys know when Josh is coming back. I'll be the first to tell you,” head coach Andy Reid said in his Monday news conference. “We’ll just see how all that works.”

Simmons appeared in eight games as a rookie in 2025.

Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has started in Simmons’ stead at left tackle and has helped keep Patrick Mahomes upright. The quarterback has been sacked just four times through the first three weeks.

item.title: Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Report says there's a "0.0 percent chance" the House passes it before election day in November.
item.content:encoded:
Big-time college sports has moved halfway toward the federal bailout they crave. The rest of the journey is unlikely to happen soon.

The U.S. Senate passed the so-called "Protect College Sports Act" on Monday night, by a vote of 77-22. The bill now goes to the U.S. House of Representatives.

Earlier in the day, Pat Forde of SI.com cited an unnamed source who said that there is a “0.0 percent chance" the House will pass the bill before the midterm elections.

With the Democrats widely expected to seize control of the House in November, the question then becomes whether it will do any meaningful business before the next Congress convenes in January.

So there's still a long way to go before the NCAA and its members get the antitrust exemption and other benefits designed to stave off a catastrophe. Even as college football is more popular and profitable than ever.

There's chaos, they say. From whose perspective? The players, after years of being exploited by a system that denied them the opportunity to participate meaningfully in the value they generate, are sitting pretty. It's not chaotic for them; it's the free market in operation.

But the schools apparently can't be trusted to balance their budgets, which is bullshit. Every American business faces an ongoing challenge to adapt or fail. In lieu of expecting the administrators to come up with a better way to carve up the pie and/or to spend within their means, they want artificial restrictions on what the players can make.

That's not how it should be. And, despite the Senate vote, maybe it won't be.

Mike Florio and Chris Simms discuss the Senate passing the Protect College Sports Act and break down the multiple factors at play in the situation.

item.title: Dolphins put De'Von Achane on injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Dolphins running back De'Von Achane's season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and the Dolphins made a roster move related to the injury on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
Dolphins running back De'Von Achane's season is over after he suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and the Dolphins made a roster move related to the injury on Monday.

Achane was placed on injured reserve as part of a series of roster moves in Miami. The Dolphins also waived defensive lineman Keith Cooper off of the 53-man roster and released defensive linemen Clelin Ferrell and Jordan Miller from the practice squad.

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said at a Monday press conference that his "heart breaks" for Achane and said that all of the team's other running backs will have roles in filling in for him.

Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon are the other backs on the 53-man roster, but the Dolphins could add to that group now that they have two open roster spots at their disposal.

item.title: J.J. McCarthy joins a small group of first-round quarterbacks who made quick exits
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Vikings have scrapped the J.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings have scrapped the J.J. McCarthy experience after the 2024 first-round pick made only 10 starts in two-plus seasons.

That adds McCarthy to a short list of first-round quarterbacks who, for whatever reason, didn't last very long with the teams that drafted them.

Via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, Elias Sports Bureau identifies only four first-round quarterbacks in the past 25 years who started 10 or fewer games for the team that picked them.

Paxton Lynch, the 2016 first-round pick of the Broncos, started only four games in Denver. He never played in a regular-season game for any other team.

Trey Lance, for whom the 49ers traded up in 2021 to make the third overall selection, started only four games in San Francisco. (He has since made eight appearances with two starts for the Cowboys and Chargers.)

Johnny Manziel, a first-round pick of the Browns in 2014, started eight games in Cleveland. He never played for another NFL team.

McCarthy had exactly 10 starts with the Vikings. He won six of them. But the Vikings have opted to take a fifth-round pick in order to move on from him.

While it's far less than the first-round pick plus more that they gave up to get him, it's more than what they would have gotten if he'd been cut before the start of the 2026 season. Which seemed to be a real possibility in late August, especially after he slipped to third on the depth chart.

Either way, the Vikings pulled the plug. And now they'll have to hope that McCarthy doesn't become the latest second-act (or third-act) quarterback who becomes a star for someone else.

Sure, the Vikings would never say it out loud. They don't need to. They know that the only thing that will make their McCarthy misadventures worse will be watching him become for someone else what the Vikings hoped he would be.

item.content:encoded:
Bears left tackle Braxton Jones is in the training room for further evaluation after a third-quarter injury.

Jones was injured on a third-down incompletion with 10:21 remaining in the quarter.

His right leg appeared to buckle on a bull rush by Jonathan Greenard, and Jones needed help getting off the field.

The Bears list Jones as questionable to return with a knee injury.

Theo Benedet replaced Jones, with Ozzy Trapilo inactive. Benedet played nine snaps in the first half, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune.

The Bears added a field goal in the third quarter, with Cairo Santos' 48-yard kick giving Chicago a 13-7 lead.

item.title: Klint Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore.
item.content:encoded:
In the battle of the offensive coordinators of the last two Super Bowl winners, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak got the better of Saints coach Kellen Moore.

The 35-27 victory moved the Raiders to 3-0. To no surprise, Kubiak is the early favorite for coach of the year.

One big reason for that is "coach of the year" typically means "coach whose team most exceeded the generally accepted preseason expectations." Under that test, it could be no one (for now) other than Kubiak.

The Raiders were 3-14 in 2025. They're now 3-0. And they've played well enough to show it's not a fluke.

Meanwhile, Kubiak has become only the third Raiders coach to launch his career with three straight wins. The others were Bill Callahan in 2002 and John Madden in 1969.

Callahan took the Raiders to the Super Bowl. Madden, in his first year, took the Raiders to the AFL Championship. If Kubiak simply takes the Raiders to the 7th seed, he'll likely be getting a trophy that his father, Gary, never won. While pursuing the possibility of having the first father-son picnic that consists of both guys showing up with a Super Bowl trophy.

item.title: Vikings send J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Minnesota send 10th pick in 2024 to New York.
item.content:encoded:
The J.J. McCarthy experiment in Minnesota has ended. In New York, it's just beginning.

Per multiple reports, the Vikings have traded the tenth overall pick in the 2024 draft to the Giants. In return, the Vikings will receive a 2027 fifth-round pick.

The Giants have a clear need at the position, given the knee injury that will keep Jaxson Dart out for at least the rest of the regular season. On Sunday, the starter was Jameis Winston, with Jake Haener as the understudy.

In Minnesota, McCarthy lost the starting job to Kyler Murray before falling behind Carson Wentz to the third spot on the depth chart. From the moment McCarthy was benched, it seemed that he was on borrowed time in Minnesota — even though everyone involved was saying all the right things.

For the Giants, the move brings the former Michigan quarterback (coached by Jim Harbaugh) to the NFL team coached by John Harbaugh.

For now, Winston is the starter. Whether McCarthy gets an opportunity to play depends on whether Winston is injured — and whether Winston remains sufficiently effective.

item.title: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley: J.J. McCarthy trade was the best decision for the Vikings
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Nolan Teasley was not the Vikings' General Manager who drafted J.J.
item.content:encoded:
Nolan Teasley was not the Vikings' General Manager who drafted J.J. McCarthy, but he became the one who ended the quarterback's time in Minnesota on Monday.

McCarthy was traded to the Giants in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and Teasley explained the decision to cut ties with the 2024 first-round pick at a press conference on Monday afternoon. Teasley said that McCarthy, who was the third-string quarterback, did not request a trade, but that the Vikings believed that making a move was "the best path forward and the best decision."

"We have a responsibility to make decisions that we believe are in the best interest of the organization, of the Vikings holistically," Teasley said. "Sometimes, those decisions aren't easy, but you just have to recognize when a different situation or a new opportunity presents itself it has the opportunity to present better outcomes.”

Teasley had spoken about McCarthy continuing to develop throughout the offseason and said that he continues "to believe that his story is not written in this league and that he has potential to continue to grow and develop and make a difference" as an NFL player, but that won't be happening in Minnesota. He also called the fifth-round pick an asset that could potentially help the Vikings this season as they could move it again in a trade before the deadline.

item.title: Nick Sirianni on Jalen Hurts medical check: "Doctors have to do their job"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was visibly frustrated by a sideline concussion evaluation that kept him off the field for a promising drive that ended in an Andy Dalton interception during Monday night's game against the Bears.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was visibly frustrated by a sideline concussion evaluation that kept him off the field for a promising drive that ended in an Andy Dalton interception during Monday night's game against the Bears. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni didn't love the moment, either, but he understands the importance of ensuring that the players are kept safe and healthy.

"Obviously frustrating," Sirianni told Lisa Salters of ESPN at halftime of Monday night's game, "but the doctors have to do their job. The guys — they got to protect these guys. And, you know, we have a hit on the sideline that they looked at, and that's the way it goes. We gotta be able to run the ball in from the one, regardless of who's in there. Yeah, I'm bummed that Jalen wasn't in for that. We got to take care of the ball with Andy. But, hey, I mean, they're doing their best to keep the players safe."

Unlike former Giants coach Brian Daboll last year in a prime-time game against the Eagles, the emotional Sirianni stayed away from the tent. The punishment imposed by the league on the Giants, Daboll, and running back Cam Skattebo may have had something to do with that.

Regardless, Sirianni gets it. If a player is getting checked for a concussion, he's not available. The coaching staff and the players have no choice but to adapt to that circumstance.

item.title: Case Keenum's second TD pass has Bears holding 20-7 lead
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bears looked like they might be in trouble early in the practice week, with their top two quarterbacks on the injury report.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears looked like they might be in trouble early in the practice week, with their top two quarterbacks on the injury report. Caleb Williams is inactive tonight with a hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent is serving as the backup after clearing concussion protocol.

But the Bears have Case Keenum, who is making his 67th career start.

He has thrown his 80th and 81st career touchdown passes tonight, with the latter giving the Bears a 20-7 lead.

Keenum hit Kalif Raymond for a 41-yard touchdown on the Eagles' busted coverage with 5:47 remaining in the third quarter.

Keenum is 22-of-29 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, and Raymond has six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown.

The Eagles began the second half with three three-and-outs and have 12 yards in the third quarter.

item.title: Monday Night Football: Case Keenum, Bears beat Eagles 27-7
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bears third-string quarterback hadn't played since 2023.
item.content:encoded:
Case Keenum, playing his first game since 2023, ran for a touchdown and threw two touchdowns in leading the Bears to a 27-7 blowout of the Eagles. Both teams are 2-1.

Despite playing without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who is out with a hamstring injury, the Bears dominated the Eagles.

Keenum, in his 67th career start, joined Ryan Fitzpatrick as the only quarterbacks to win starts for seven different NFL teams.

He threw an 8-yard touchdown to Luther Burden and a 41-yarder to Kalif Raymond. A 6-yard touchdown pass to Colston Loveland was overturned on replay, with the tight end just short of the goal line. Keenum ended the team's scoring in the fourth quarter with a 1-yard touchdown run on third down.

Keenum went 24-of-34 for 247 yards. Raymond caught six passes for 90 yards, and Burden added seven for 61.

The Bears outgained the Eagles 375 to 248 yards and held the ball for 36:53.

Philadelphia never led.

The Eagles did close to within 10-7 at halftime, with Jalen Hurts scoring on the tush push on the final play of the half. Philadelphia, though, opened the second half with three consecutive three-and-outs and 12 total yards.

The Eagles, who had 62 yards in the second half, shot themselves in the cleat all night.

Andy Dalton, who briefly replaced Hurts after the starter was pulled out of the game for a concussion check, threw an interception into the end zone from the 2-yard line. It was rookie Dillon Thieneman's first career pick.

Hurts threw an interception at the Chicago 46; Tank Bigsby lost a fumble at his own 15; the Eagles were 2-of-9 on third downs; and they committed 10 penalties, including four on defense.

Hurts went 16-of-25 for 153 yards and an interception, with DeVonta Smith catching six for 65. Saquon Barkley had 15 rushes for 82 yards.

item.title: Ben Johnson praises Case Keenum, doesn't say who Bears' starting QB will be next week
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: With Caleb Williams recovering from a hamstring injury, the Bears may turn to Tyson Bagent Sunday against the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Bears head coach Ben Johnson praised third-string quarterback Case Keenum after Monday night's win over the Eagles, but Johnson wasn't ready to say whether Keenum will start again on Sunday against the Jets.

"It's all about Case Keenum," Johnson said. "What he was able to do here tonight, I thought he did an extraordinary job. When the running game's not going, being able to lean into the passing game as a play caller . . . He played really efficient football and I couldn't be more proud of him for that."

Keenum started against the Eagles because Caleb Williams is out with a hamstring injury and second-string quarterback Tyson Bagent spent most of the week in the league's concussion protocol. Bagent was active as the Bears' No. 2 quarterback, and Johnson said it's too soon to say whether Bagent will be No. 1 against the Jets.

"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said. "But I said it last week and I'll say it again: There was a reason Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."

Johnson said the Bears have three quarterbacks they can win with.

"Whether it's Caleb, whether it's Tyson, whether it's Case," Johnson said, "we've got one of the best quarterback rooms in the NFL."

item.title: PFT's Week 4 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's a new sheriff in town (and they're dressed like 1960s Batman).
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 2; 3-0): The Bills are No. 1, but the Adam West Batman uniforms would be No. 32.

2. Chiefs (No. 4; 3-0): The Chiefs are back . . . to playing with their food before winning easily.

3. 49ers (No. 5; 3-0): They're dropping like flies but still winning every week.

4. Broncos (No. 6; 2-1): The Rams let the Broncos hang around just long enough to steal it.

5. Jaguars (No. 7; 2-1): Get used to the possibility of seeing a lot of teal in L.A. during Super Bowl week.

6. Seahawks (No. 1; 2-1): We'll find out soon whether the loss at Washington was an aberration or a harbinger.

7. Bengals (No. 3; 2-1): You can't beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh by repeatedly shooting yourself in the foot.

8. Rams (No. 9; 1-2): With the Eagles and Bills coming up, the Rams need to flush Sunday night's outcome quickly.

9. Vikings (No. 11; 3-0): Just when it looked like they may need J.J. McCarthy at some point this season, they traded him.

10. Bears (No. 12; 2-1): They should ride with Case Keenum until Caleb Williams returns.

11. Eagles (No. 8; 2-1): Who misses A.J. Brown more? His current team or his former one?

12. Ravens (No. 13; 2-1): Great teams win games they feel destined to lose.

13. Steelers (No. 18; 2-1): There's some magic left in the post-Tomlin Steelers.

14. Lions (No. 16; 2-1): The defense still isn't nearly good enough.

15. Raiders (No. 22; 3-0): Kirk-3-and-oh Chainz.

16. Giants (No. 17; 2-1): How long will Jameis Winston hold the starting job?

17. Texans (No. 10; 0-3): The offense needed to get a little bit better. Instead, the defense got more than a little bit worse.

18. Browns (No. 23; 2-1): The Browns isn't the Browns.

19. Saints (No. 15; 1-2): It's unclear how many games they'll win, but all of them will be fun to watch.

20. Patriots (No. 14; 1-2): There was blood on the ball; now there's blood in the water.

21. Cowboys (No. 20; 1-2): How long until they can start building hype for 2027?

22. Falcons (No. 32; 1-2): Michael Penix Jr. was ready to go, just in the nick of time.

23. Commanders (No. 30; 1-2): Marcus Mariota's performance will accelerate Jayden Daniels's return.

24. Colts (No. 27; 1-2): The losing streak is over, but the Colts are still a long way from being back to what they were before last year's collapse.

25. Packers (No. 19; 1-2): The shareholders should consider a hostile takeover.

26. Panthers (No. 21; 1-2): We're learning that winning the NFC South last season doesn't mean much.

27. Cardinals (No. 24; 1-2): Reality has quickly settled in.

28. Jets (No. 28; 1-2): They'll never be a contender until they can win games they're supposed to lose.

29. Chargers (No. 25; 0-3): Justin Herbert has replaced Joe Burrow as the "veteran QB most likely to change teams in 2027."

30. Buccaneers (No. 26; 0-3): Raymond James Stadium could be Lambeau South when the Packers come to town on Sunday.

31. Titans (No. 29; 0-3): If Cam Ward is the real deal, he needs to start showing it real soon.

32. Dolphins (No. 31; 0-3): Stephen Ross won't need to offer Jeff Hafley $100,000 for each game the team loses.

item.title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward made a bad decision, but he isn't reckless
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: After quarterback Cam Ward threw an interception in the end zone late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that Ward has "to be smarter with the football."
item.content:encoded:
After quarterback Cam Ward threw an interception in the end zone late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that Ward has "to be smarter with the football."

Saleh spent more time discussing Ward's decision making during his Monday press conference. Saleh said that he thinks Ward has been "spot on" with his decisions in most respects, which makes it "unfortunate that one of his critical mistakes came on the last play of the game" but does not make Ward a reckless player with the ball.

"He gave him a bad ball," Saleh said, via the team's website. "Bad decision, not a reckless decision, bad decision, which I'm sure he recognizes. But Cam is far from reckless."

Recklessness may not be Ward's chief issue, but the simple fact for the Titans is that their offense is not productive enough to overcome even an occasional mistake. They've scored 37 points in three weeks and that number is going to need to climb for Ward to have a compelling case that he's the long-term answer in Tennessee.

item.title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward has to be smarter with the football
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Titans had the ball inside the Giants' 10-yard-line with 24 seconds left in Sunday's game, but any hopes of a comeback win were dashed when quarterback Cam Ward's final pass left his hand.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans had the ball inside the Giants' 10-yard-line with 24 seconds left in Sunday's game, but any hopes of a comeback win were dashed when quarterback Cam Ward's final pass left his hand.

Ward rolled left and had room to run for at least a short gain before getting out of bounds or using one of the Titans' two timeouts. Ward made a different choice, though, and tried to float a pass to wide receiver Elic Ayomanor in the back of the end zone. Giants safety Jevon Holland was in front of Ayomanor, however, and he made a jumping interception to seal a 12-7 Giants win.

Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's angry reaction in the booth was caught on camera and head coach Robert Saleh took issue with the decision in his postgame press conference.

"He’s out in the open field, just be smarter with the football," Saleh said. "We’ve got two timeouts left, it’s first and goal on the 8. We’re gonna score, you don’t need to force it in that situation. Unfortunately it happened."

Ward said he didn't think the throw was "reckless," but the response from the coaches showed a different analysis. Saleh said his issues with that decision and Ward's overall play have not led him to consider to benching the first overall pick of the 2025 draft, but some clear signs of growth from the offense would be welcomed in Tennessee.

item.title: Jaguars got football from Travis Hunter's first interception after sideline squabble
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter's first NFL interception helped Jacksonville beat the Patriots on Sunday, but it also touched off an odd scene on the sideline.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter's first NFL interception helped Jacksonville beat the Patriots on Sunday, but it also touched off an odd scene on the sideline.

Hunter spun the ball on the ground while celebrating the takeaway and teammate Josh Hines-Allen tried to retrieve it as a souvenir from a Patriots ballboy who had picked it up. Video of the interaction showed Hines-Allen trying to take the ball, which was zealously protected by the ballboy who shouted that Hines-Allen should not touch him. A Jaguars staffer eventually stepped in and the game went on.

During a videoconference on Monday, Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said the team was working to get the ball for Hunter.

"I was just talking about it," Coen said, via Mark Long of the Associated Press. "I haven't gotten a clean answer. We've been in communication with those guys over there. I think they've gotten it sorted out; I can't say for certain if we got the actual ball or not. I know there was something that went on there. I think it's all squared away. We'll get it taken care of."

Cornerback Jourdan Lewis noted that Hunter "could have helped us out by not spinning the ball and forgetting about it," but the Jaguars later confirmed that they were able to secure the ball.

item.title: Kevin O'Connell: We're going to improve, ascend as an offense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Vikings are 3-0, but it isn't because they have found an offensive groove so far this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings are 3-0, but it isn't because they have found an offensive groove so far this season.

In three weeks of work, they have managed to pick up a league-worst 715 yards and their passing game has been the least productive in the league. That didn't stop them from trading quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on Monday and head coach Kevin O'Connell expressed confidence later in the day that starter Kyler Murray will be able to create better results with more time in the offense.

"Look, we've seen Kyler play 11 snaps in one game and played against a good defense on the road yesterday. There's a lot of things beyond Kyler that we need to improve, including myself, and we're going to do that, and we're going to ascend as an offense," O'Connell said, via the team's website. "I believe in our guys. I believe in where we can get to as a team, and I just love the fact that collectively we're able to come together and find a way to win football games."

Things got particularly bleak for the Vikings in the second half in Tampa on Sunday as they gained 77 yards and picked up four first downs while turning the ball over once and punting four times. A game against the winless Dolphins this week gives the Vikings a chance to find some better footing and questions about when that will happen will get a bit more pointed if they continue to scuffle the way they did against the Buccaneers.

item.title: Eagles defense has to "get on the same page" after loss to Bears
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When the Eagles faced the Bears in 2025, they gave up 281 rushing yards in a Black Friday loss.
item.content:encoded:
When the Eagles faced the Bears in 2025, they gave up 281 rushing yards in a Black Friday loss.

The Eagles had more success against the Chicago rushing attack on Monday night, but the result wasn't any better. Bears third-string quarterback Case Keenum was never sacked and rarely pressured while going 24-of-34 for 247 yards and two touchdowns in his first start since the 2023 season.

Missed tackles were an issue somewhat obscured by wins in the first two weeks of the season and that remained a problem for a defense that has yet to force a turnover this season. Add that to breakdowns in coverage that led to big plays like a Kalif Raymond touchdown catch and there's a lot for the unit to work on.

Defensive back Cooper DeJean chalked that Raymond touchdown up to "miscommunication" and said the defense needs to focus on cleaning that up first.

“We just got to get on the same page,” DeJean said, via Jeff Neiburg of the Philadelphia Inquirer.

Week 4 brings a date with the Rams on a short week, so that work will have to begin right away for the Eagles to put themselves on better footing in the future.

item.title: Nick Sirianni regrets his emotional outburst after hit on Jalen Hurts
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Sirianni appeared to be screaming at Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles coach Nick Sirianni appeared to be screaming obscenities toward Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson after a hit on quarterback Jalen Hurts that forced Hurts to leave the game for a concussion evaluation on Monday night. Afterward, Sirianni regretted it.

Sirianni said after the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears that he doesn't think Jackson, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness, was trying to make a dirty play.

"You want to always fight for your players and protect your players," Sirianni said. "I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse. 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me.' Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline. It ended up being a penalty, obviously you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that. But it's in the heat of the moment, I know nobody is trying to hurt anybody out there, and I always have remorse when I act that way. But I always love fighting for our players. I love our guys. So the emotion of the game probably got the better of me today and I have to learn from that. In that particular moment I have to be more steady in that situation. Be able to move on and go to the next play. I didn't like how I handled that."

Sirianni was critical of himself in his post-game comments, saying he got out-coached. After the Eagles' first loss, Sirianni has some things he needs to work on.

item.title: Sean McVay apologizes for Sunday night press conference cameo
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday night's Rams-Broncos game had an interesting postscript arising from coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night's Rams-Broncos game had an interesting postscript arising from coach Sean McVay's postgame press conference. It was short, mainly because he started and finished before the bulk of the reporters covering the team could get to the media room.

On Monday, McVay opened his day-after availability with an apology.

“I’m sorry that I missed you guys yesterday," McVay said, via a transcript provided by the team. "I had been going for a few minutes and there was some misunderstanding with some of the timing. Once a question was asked, there was enough silence [for the press conference to end].

"It never was my intention to ever miss any of your questions. If there was any sort of misunderstanding, that was definitely not the case. I apologize for that, but [V.P. of communications] Artis [Twyman] just made me aware of that. I understand my role and responsibilities to be able to talk, whether it's after a win or whether we don't get the results that we want. I want to at least acknowledge that. I know a couple of our beat reporters were just — there was a mix-up with timing, but I was in there for a few minutes. There was a pause in any sort of questions and obviously, [it was an] emotional game. That was what led to that, but if there was any misinterpretation, I do apologize for that."

It's good that McVay apologized. Still, it's hard to imagine McVay doing a 90-second cameo if the Rams had won the game.

We saw and heard a blunt and feisty McVay last December, after a tough, hard-fought game against the Seahawks. He's intense. He's emotional.

Ultimately, he's human. And while, in most circumstances, he's able to keep those emotions in check, he may have said something he didn't want to say if he'd been given repeated chances to talk about some of the calls that were made down the stretch on Sunday night.
